R01.why: The question needs only one example of any kind, so this one specific external source (transport links) is never required — and the question does not even signal external over internal economies.

R02.why: Explaining what economies of scale means is exactly the statement that long-run average cost falls as scale rises, so the long-run cost curve relationship is the substance of the explanation.

R03.why: X-inefficiency is one of the listed sources of diseconomies of scale and is directly responsive to an 'examine the reasons why' ask, which calls for the sources as a set rather than one arbitrary instance.

R04.why: Communication problems are a core listed source of diseconomies of scale and are precisely the kind of reason the question asks the student to examine.

R05.why: Calculating total variable cost is short-run cost arithmetic and contributes nothing to explaining why long-run unit costs rise with scale.

R06.why: Coordination problems are a listed source of diseconomies of scale and sit squarely within the set of reasons the question demands.

R07.why: Marginal revenue is a revenue concept with no bearing on defining economies of scale or giving an example of one.

R08.why: The average product / average cost link is short-run productivity theory (diminishing returns), a different question from long-run diseconomies of scale, and conflating the two is a standard error rather than a requirement here.

R09.why: To show the reasons are diseconomies of scale at all, the answer has to carry each one through to rising long-run average cost, which is this relationship — though the reasons themselves, not the curve, are the main ask.
